items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: And that's Shabby Willis-Ranger. She's got the closet. ... And we did a recording date there. For Decca, I think, or Columbia.

ctx.x: Now this is sing, this is must be made later. Later, later, later. Yeah, yeah. Well, they made a lot of little one-wheel. I remember that you were in there. Yeah, yeah.

I mean, there was. I don't know, but I don't remember this one. Now, when I was with the big man in California, we played at Sam Sebastian's Cotton Club. They had two reviews, the color review and the white review for two months. Louie was in the phone, man. We recorded that. The skeleton in the closet. Yeah. And all that. And that's Shabby Willis-Ranger. She's got the closet. What the hell was a random. And we did a recording date there. For Decca, I think, or Columbia. It must have been Decca. Decca. And that…
That's a number that Lee Collins played when he came up to your club on the excursion. Remember? Mm-hmm. The saxophone player was telling us about Lee coming up there and playing that number.
